title: Coronation Chicken Salad
subtitle: chicken in a curried mayonnaise dressing
excerpt: Coronation chicken was created for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation lunch in 1953. Poached chicken goes into a dressing of mayonnaise, cream, and curry spices with a hint of sweetness from mango chutney. It is a British classic that still works as well as it did when it was invented.
sourceNotes: Created by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation banquet in 1953. It has become one of the most recognisable British salad dishes.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Good for sandwiches and jacket potatoes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to a day ahead. The flavour improves as it sits.

content.text: Poach the chicken gently -- a rolling boil will toughen it. Let it cool in the cooking liquid so it stays moist. Shred with two forks or cut into chunks.

items.prepNote: serve on a bed of salad leaves

content.text: Put the chicken breasts in a pan with the onion, bay leaves, and cold water to cover. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through.
Remove from the heat. Let the chicken cool in the liquid for 10 minutes. Drain, then shred or cut into chunks.
Mix the mayonnaise, cream, garam masala, mango chutney, lemon juice, and celery in a bowl. Season with salt.
Fold the chicken into the dressing. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve on a bed of salad leaves. Garnish with a few toasted flaked almonds if you have them.

items.cause: Overcooked or not cooled in liquid
items.fix: Poach gently and leave in the liquid as it cools -- this keeps it moist.
Add more lemon juice to balance.

content.text: Coronation chicken was created in 1953 for the banquet following Queen Elizabeth II's coronation. The dish was developed by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume of the Cordon Bleu Cookery School. It reflected post-war Britain's growing interest in Indian-influenced flavours. It has since become a British staple served at everything from garden parties to school lunches.
